statements.text: Obviously, we have a lot we have to learn because we have to figure out how to not limit this technology but to manage its use.
statements.venue: Senate HSGAC subcommittee hearing, Advanced Technology: Examining Threats to National Security

statements.text: We have to be able to build on a value set of what is responsible AI, and then work from there.
Much of the AI conversation really boils around not just a responsible use but the data that is behind it.
statements.context: Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs hearing on AI in Government, May 16, 2023.

statements.text: Privacy is losing the battle when it comes to allowing AI. https://t.co/dpEmR8Qcuv

The most difficult thing that I continue to be able to hear is the continual term everyone throws around, we just want to make sure there is responsible use of AI, to which I always smile and say, define that for me. I have yet to have anyone be able to really wrap a good definition of what responsible use of AI means and does not mean. [...] Does anyone want to try to jump in on that and give me a concise definition of what responsible use of AI means?
statements.context: Senate hearing on governing AI through acquisition and procurement, where Senator Lankford presses witnesses for a definition of 'responsible use of AI.'

statements.text: We have another big challenge in the Federal acquisition procurement process that deals with software is who owns the intellectual property. Because if we do weapon systems, there is just, we are going to keep updating it, and we have to know this. With AI, it becomes particularly difficult on who owns the intellectual property for this and when changes need to be made. How do you know that you have a safe process to be able to do updates on this?
statements.context: Senate hearing on governing AI through federal acquisition and procurement, with Senator Lankford questioning witnesses on regulatory frameworks and procurement challenges.

statements.text: That is uniquely challenging with AI, because we have to get into how has it been trained, what is the decisionmaking and the process, how do we verify that decisionmaking process when we are verifying it for security, for biases, for all those things?
statements.context: Senate hearing on governing AI through federal acquisition and procurement, with Senator Lankford questioning witnesses about verification challenges for AI systems purchased by the government.

statements.text: Define the phrase responsible AI for me, because everyone seems to throw around, we want to make sure we have a responsible AI. But this is not a trick question. I am really trying to figure out how is that defined—what does that mean, responsible AI? How do we start to define that?
statements.context: Senate hearing on advanced technology and national security, Senator Lankford questioning expert witnesses.

statements.text: We're in a unique position now, where the PRC is also very interested in partnering, and there are current research hubs in the PRC on Open AI that Google and Microsoft both have at this point. The question is, how far does that go and what do we engage with and at what point does that become facilitating someone who may be an economic adversary, that we hope is never a military adversary in that kind of partnership of that kind of research?
statements.context: Senator Lankford questioning witnesses at an Open Hearing of the Senate Intelligence Committee on the national security implications of AI.

statements.text: If we are going to upload that data to any one of these private entities, the question then becomes, once we hand data over for machine learning—we have handed a lot of data over. Who owns that data? Where does that data go?
statements.context: Senate hearing on advanced technology and national-security threats, where Senator Lankford poses questions about data sharing and AI governance.

statements.text: If you've got a satellite part, piece, or satellite as a whole, it's already been developed, already used.
statements.context: Senator Lankford speaks during an open Senate Intelligence Committee hearing on the national security implications of AI.

statements.text: I get it. [...] you cannot go beyond here, if that makes sense.
statements.context: Senate hearing on advanced technology and national security threats, featuring Senator Lankford discussing the need for AI statutory frameworks.

statements.text: Americans’ data is all over the internet—with the growth of AI we need to keep Americans’ information safe. https://t.co/uZVLfXx3qw

We passed and made law the TAKE IT DOWN Act. This is about the revenge porn that we are seeing that has affected so many young lives. They are posting their images and sometimes using AI to destroy the lives of people they either hate, used to date, or whatever it may be.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Senator James Lankford reviewing legislative accomplishments during the first seven months of the Trump presidency.

statements.text:
Proud to join a bipartisan group of colleagues calling on AI companies to commit to real transparency and safety disclosures. As AI becomes more powerful, we need to protect children and vulnerable users. Innovation comes with responsibility.

https://t.co/M5bFQTf9NL
What counsel is that AI going to do? These are hard issues we’re going to deal with as culture, but they’re also legislative issues. What will AI feed my kids?
statements.venue: Tulsa Flyer article on remarks about AI regulation

statements.text: Trust has to be earned, and right now families are being asked to trust AI companies with very little information. The AI Systems Transparency Act gives parents and consumers the straightforward answers on how these AI models are built and how they interact with America’s children. Transparency on innovation earns the public’s trust.
statements.venue: Senate press release on AI Systems Transparency Act

statements.text: Religious freedom is the first freedom in our Constitution. It protects the right of every person to have a faith, live their faith, change their faith, or have no faith at all. AI is a system that researches ideas, opinions, and facts, but it is not the final word on faith. On issues of faith, AI systems should send users to the sacred texts and to the faith leaders who have walked with people through joy and grief for generations.
statements.venue: Senate press release on AI religious freedom resolution

statements.text: AI is not the enemy, and I don’t believe AI is going to create the Terminator and come shoot us [...] It (AI) is coming and if we don’t develop it faster than our enemies, they will learn our vulnerabilities before we will and will exploit them.
